_doc: Skeleton index — organized by families (argument type) with emphasis variants. The matcher reads this single file. Flow: intake fingerprint → match family → detect/ask emphasis → pick variant → load that variant's contract.

families.description: Diagnostic arc — names a problem, explains its root cause(s), proposes a fix

signals: prompt contains a problem/loss/cost/risk AND its cause/driver/reason AND an action/fix/recommendation
quantifiable negative impact
cause can be decomposed into 2-4 segments

cause_visual_options._doc: The cause zone uses swappable chart types. Each skeleton defaults to one; the builder matches based on data shape.

ranked-bars.data_fit: magnitude — independent drivers ranked by absolute value

trend-bars.data_fit: temporal — cause is a worsening trend over time

emphasis_question.prompt: What should the reader focus on first?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user says 'convince to act' or 'get approval' → decision. If 'understand why' or 'root cause' → cause. If 'how bad is it' or 'impact' → impact. If unclear → ask.

options.label: Balanced view
options.description: Equal weight across problem, cause, and fix

options.label: The financial impact
options.description: Lead with the cost — hero stat dominates, cause and fix are supporting

options.label: The root cause
options.description: Lead with the breakdown — cause analysis is the hero, flanked by problem and fix

options.label: The decision
options.description: Lead with the action options — what to do is the hero, problem and cause are context

variants.name: 3-column equal weight
variants.layout: 3 equal columns: problem | cause | fix. Each has hero stat + claim + detail content. Progression strip at bottom.

variants.name: Impact hero with cause/fix sidebar
variants.layout: 58/42 split. Left: 72px hero stat + claim + 2 supporting stats. Right: stacked cause (ranked horizontal bars by magnitude) + fix (action steps). Summary bar at bottom.

variants.name: Cause breakdown hero
variants.layout: Full-width cause segmented bar (36px) as hero in surface panel with aligned legend. Below: 2-column grid — left problem stat + context, right fix stat + action steps. Callout band at bottom.

variants.name: Decision-forward with context rail
variants.layout: Left 35%: context rail with problem stat + cause trend mini-chart (6-quarter vertical bars). Right 65%: 2 option zone-cards side by side, each with badge + title + metric + bullets. Decision callout at bottom.

families.description: Value walk — start → drivers (gains/drags) → end. Classic bridge or margin decomposition.

signals: prompt describes change from one value to another
names specific drivers/factors explaining the change
has start and end values with contributing items

emphasis_question.prompt: What matters more about this walk?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user focuses on 'what drove the change' → drivers. If 'where we ended up' → outcome. If 'what went wrong' → drags.

options.label: Full bridge
options.description: Equal weight — start, all drivers, end shown proportionally

options.label: Driver deep-dive
options.description: Chart is hero, findings annotate the top 2-3 drivers

options.label: Outcome focus
options.description: End value is the hero stat, bridge is supporting context

variants.name: 60/40 waterfall + annotated findings
variants.layout: Left 60%: waterfall chart with labeled bars. Right 40%: 2-3 analyst findings with chips.

variants.name: Executive waterfall with action strip
variants.layout: Full-width CSS waterfall hero with running-total connectors + bracket annotation. Callout band + 3-step action strip below.

families.description: Items ranked or composed by value — who's biggest, what's the mix, where's the concentration.

signals: prompt lists items with comparable values
natural ordering by magnitude
concentration or dominance pattern

emphasis_question.prompt: What's the story in the ranking?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user highlights a gap between top and rest → dominance. If distribution matters → spread. If comparing two groups → split.

options.label: Top-heavy
options.description: Lead item dominates — hero stat is the leader, bar chart shows the drop-off

options.label: Even spread
options.description: Distribution is the story — all items shown proportionally, no single hero

options.label: Two-group contrast
options.description: Top group vs bottom group — visual split emphasizes the divide

variants.name: Ranked bar chart + annotated rail
variants.layout: Left 55%: horizontal ranked bar chart with stats line. Right 45%: compact data table + findings rail with semantic chips. Summary bar at bottom.

variants.name: Horizontal ranking with detail rows
variants.layout: 55/45 split. Left: three-tier ranked bars with vs-avg delta badges + spread summary line. Right: data table + findings rail. Spread-emphasis: quantifies range and ratio.

families.description: Performance vs a reference point — industry benchmark, competitor, prior period, target.

signals: prompt compares values against a benchmark or reference
has 'vs', 'compared to', 'relative to', 'gap'
named reference entity (industry, competitor, target)

emphasis_question.prompt: What matters more — where you stand or the gap?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user asks 'how do we compare' → position. If 'how far behind' or 'what to close' → gap.

options.label: Competitive position
options.description: Side-by-side comparison — reader sees relative standing

options.label: Gap to close
options.description: Delta is the hero — reader sees what needs to change

variants.name: Margin comparison with benchmark line
variants.layout: 55/45 split. Left: hero gap stat + horizontal bars with benchmark markers + gap badges. Right: findings with bridge text + action block. Consultant credibility sourcing.

families.description: Stages, phases, or steps in a sequence — pipeline, lifecycle, methodology, flywheel.

signals: prompt describes sequential stages or phases
has step 1/2/3 or phase language
describes a pipeline, workflow, or methodology

emphasis_question.prompt: Is this about the overall system or a specific bottleneck?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user focuses on one broken step → bottleneck. If describing the whole approach → system. If showing adoption → progress.

options.label: Full system view
options.description: All stages shown equally — reader sees the whole process

options.label: Bottleneck focus
options.description: One stage is called out — reader sees where it breaks

options.label: Progress tracking
options.description: Stages shown with done/current/next status

variants.name: Flywheel with thesis banner
variants.layout: Circular flywheel diagram with thesis banner above. Stage labels around the ring.

variants.name: Trend chart with KPI strip
variants.layout: Full-width stacked bar chart as hero. KPI stat-row below chart. Optional annotation marker.

variants.name: Pipeline funnel with bottleneck callout
variants.layout: Narrowing funnel diagram. Bottleneck stage highlighted. Findings annotate the drop-off.

families.description: New capability, product, or initiative — what it is, why it matters, what changes.

signals: prompt announces something new
has 'launching', 'introducing', 'new capability', 'rolling out'
describes what it does + why it matters

emphasis_question.prompt: What should land first — the product or the impact?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user wants to show the UI → product. If they want to argue for adoption → impact.

options.label: Product showcase
options.description: Screenshot/mockup is the hero — messaging supports it

options.label: Impact argument
options.description: Benefits are the hero — product visual is supporting

variants.name: Icon-text stack + product mockup
variants.layout: Left 46%: icon-text messaging blocks. Right 54%: product image placeholder. Callout band below.

families.description: Internal alignment — thesis, strategic pillars, goals, rationale. For team buy-in, not external audiences.

signals: prompt describes strategy, priorities, or pillars
has 'our approach', 'strategic priorities', 'key pillars'
internal audience, not client-facing

emphasis_question.prompt: Is this about the big picture or the specific priorities?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user wants alignment on direction → thesis. If listing specific workstreams → pillars.

options.label: Thesis-first
options.description: Lead with the overarching strategy, pillars support it

options.label: Pillar-first
options.description: Lead with the workstreams, thesis is context

variants.name: Thesis banner + strategy pillars
variants.layout: Thesis banner with formula visual + 3 strategy pillar columns with numbered items + summary bar.

families.description: 1-slide proposal — business need, proposed solution, recommended approach. The slide that closes deals.

signals: prompt asks for an executive summary or 1-slide overview of an engagement
has 'business need', 'proposed solution', 'approach', 'executive summary'
three-part arc: what's wrong, what we'll do, how we'll do it

emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user emphasizes the pain/cost → problem. If the solution design → solution. If the engagement model → approach. If equal weight → balanced.

options.label: Equal weight
options.description: Need, solution, and approach shown side by side — reader follows the arc

options.label: The business pain
options.description: Problem metrics dominate — solution and approach are supporting

options.label: The solution design
options.description: Solution details are the hero — problem is context, approach is footer

options.label: The engagement model
options.description: Timeline and scope dominate — problem and solution are compact context

variants.name: Stat row + 3-column need/solution/approach
variants.layout: Context bar at top. Stat row (4 KPIs) as hero. Below: 3-column findings grid — Business Need | Proposed Solution | Recommended Approach. Action column in orange accent.

families.description: Side-by-side old state → new state with delta callouts. Proposals, restructured deals, timeline compression.

signals: prompt compares a previous/old/current state to a new/updated/proposed state
has 'before/after', 'previous vs updated', 'old → new', 'compressed', 'restructured'
quantifiable deltas between the two states (cost, time, scope)

emphasis_question.prompt: What should the reader focus on?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user emphasizes savings/reduction → savings. If restructured responsibilities → ownership. If equal weight → balanced.

options.label: Full comparison
options.description: Equal weight — both states shown with deltas between them

options.label: The savings
options.description: Delta callouts dominate — reader sees the improvement first

options.label: The new structure
options.description: After-state scope cards dominate — reader sees who owns what

variants.name: Decision story — comparison rows + narrative + ownership
variants.layout: Left 46%: comparison table (label | previous | delta | updated). Right 54%: narrative + process models + ownership split. Bottom: neutral hairline strip.

variants.name: Savings-hero with before/after context
variants.layout: Hero delta stats across top. Below: compact before/after comparison as supporting context.

variants.name: Ownership-forward with compact deltas
variants.layout: Large ownership cards as hero (60%). Compact before/after KPI strip and deltas as sidebar (40%).

families.description: Same starting point, materially different outcomes — the spread itself is the problem. Pricing, performance, compliance gaps across comparable entities.

signals: prompt has a single starting value/input that produces multiple different outcomes
variance or spread is not explained by the obvious variable (size, volume, tier)
entities can be compared on multiple dimensions (price, discount, margin)
the pattern suggests ad-hoc or inconsistent processes, not market forces

emphasis_question.prompt: What should the reader focus on first?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user says 'show the spread' or 'how different' → spread. If 'why is this happening' or 'root cause' → drivers. If unclear → balanced.

options.label: Balanced view
options.description: Equal weight across the spread, its drivers, and the fix

options.label: The spread itself
options.description: Lead with the visual divergence — how far apart the outcomes are

options.label: What's driving it
options.description: Lead with the mechanism — why identical inputs produce different outputs

variants.name: Divergence flow with findings rail
variants.layout: 52/48 split. Left: source orb → fork → 3 outcome orbs with entity cards. Right: finding title + drivers + quote + action card with chips.

variants.name: Scatter chart + data table with findings
variants.layout: 55/45 split. Left: scatter plot (Y=variance metric, X=size metric) with labeled data points + compact 5-column data table. Right: 3 semantic-dot findings + stakeholder quotes + action block.

variants.name: Benchmark bars with gap badges
variants.layout: 55/45 split. Left: hero gap stat + two benchmark bar panels (primary + consequence metric) with gap badges + interpretation line. Right: 3 findings with bridge text + numbered action steps.

variants.name: Spread hero — full-width divergence flow with compact driver strip
variants.layout: Full-width divergence flow as hero (65% height). Larger orbs, spread callout bracket on right edge. Below: 2-column strip — left drivers (compact), right action card.

variants.name: Drivers hero — ranked bars with context rail
variants.layout: 38/62 split (inverted). Left context rail: compact source strip + outcome rows with mini orbs + spread badge. Right hero: finding title + ranked driver bars with magnitude + quote + action card.

families.description: Key findings from an assessment — 3-5 sourced findings, each with supporting data and a client bridge. The bread-and-butter consultant deliverable.

signals: prompt presents multiple findings or observations from an assessment/review
each finding has supporting data or evidence
no dominant visual (chart, diagram) — the structured findings ARE the deliverable
no diagnostic arc (not problem→cause→fix) — just: here is what we found
prompt compares metrics against targets/benchmarks but the structured findings ARE the deliverable (not a benchmark chart)

emphasis_question.prompt: How should the findings be weighted?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If the user highlights one dominant finding → hero-finding. If the user emphasizes what to do about it → action-forward. If all findings are equally important → balanced.

options.label: Equal weight
options.description: All findings shown equally in a grid — reader scans the full picture

options.label: Lead finding
options.description: One key finding is elevated as the hero — the rest support it

options.label: Action-forward
options.description: Findings are compact context — the recommendation block dominates

variants.name: KPI strip + 3-column findings grid
variants.layout: Full-width KPI strip (3 stats). Below: 3-column findings cards with semantic accent bars + bridge text + source citations. Action band at bottom.

variants.name: Hero finding + supporting cards
variants.layout: Lead finding as hero card (full-width, large stat). Below: 2-column supporting finding cards. Compact action strip.

variants.name: Compact findings + dominant action block
variants.layout: Compact 3-column finding summaries (title + key stat only). Action block takes 40% of slide with detailed steps and timeline.

families.description: Capability scoring against a maturity model — where you are, where peers are, what's dragging the score down.

signals: prompt scores capabilities against a maturity model or readiness scale
has 'maturity', 'readiness', 'capability assessment', 'score X out of Y'
compares current state to a target or peer benchmark on a defined scale

emphasis_question.prompt: What should the reader focus on first?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If 'where do we stand' → position. If 'what's holding us back' → gaps. If 'what do we do about it' → action.

options.label: Current position
options.description: Maturity track is the hero — reader sees where they sit on the scale

options.label: Capability gaps
options.description: Capability breakdown bars are the hero — reader sees which dimensions drag the score

options.label: Closing the gap
options.description: Action plan dominates — maturity track and scores are compact context

variants.name: Maturity track + capability bars + findings
variants.layout: 55/45 split. Left: maturity stage track (5 stages, current + target highlighted) with gap badge, capability score bars below. Right: 3 findings + action block.

variants.name: Capability bars hero with compact maturity rail
variants.layout: Full-width capability bar chart as hero (ranked worst-first, target lines). Compact maturity stage strip above. Findings + action below.

variants.name: Action roadmap with compact maturity context
variants.layout: Left 40%: compact maturity track + overall score + capability sparklines. Right 60%: sequenced action cards with target score and priority rationale.

families.description: Quick-reference data — rate cards, fee schedules, conversion tables. The data IS the deliverable.

signals: prompt presents a table of reference values (rates, fees, thresholds, parameters)
has 'rate card', 'fee schedule', 'conversion table', 'reference', 'fixed rates'
reader needs to find a specific value quickly, not follow a narrative

emphasis_question.prompt: What matters more — the data or why it's set this way?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If just needs the numbers → data. If explain methodology → rationale. If one row is key → highlight.

options.label: Data-first
options.description: Table dominates — rationale is a sidebar for context

options.label: Rationale-first
options.description: Equal weight — table and methodology shown side by side

options.label: Key-row callout
options.description: One row or value is the hero — the rest is supporting context

variants.name: Data table + rationale sidebar
variants.layout: 50/50 split. Left: styled data table with header row, base-row highlight, footnote. Right: rationale header + 3-4 rationale items. Action band at bottom.

variants.name: Methodology-forward with compact table
variants.layout: Left 55%: methodology title + 4 rationale cards. Right 45%: compact data table. Callout band at bottom.

families.description: Performance tracked over time periods — quarterly revenue, monthly pipeline, annual headcount.

signals: prompt has values for the same metric across 3+ time periods
has 'quarterly', 'monthly', 'Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4', 'year-over-year', 'trend'
multiple series or categories tracked over the same time axis

emphasis_question.prompt: What's the story in the trend?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If one series growing/shrinking → focal-series. If mix shifting → mix-shift. If showing trajectory → trajectory.

options.label: Full trajectory
options.description: Stacked chart + data table — reader sees all series over all periods

options.label: One series stands out
options.description: Chart highlights the focal series — hero stat + findings explain why

options.label: Mix is shifting
options.description: Composition change is the story — share percentages and mix-shift callouts dominate

variants.name: Stacked bar chart + data table + findings rail
variants.layout: 55/45 split. Left: stacked bar chart with legend + KPI strip. Right: data table with Δ column + findings with semantic chips. Summary bar at bottom.

variants.name: Focal series hero with contribution context
variants.layout: 58/42 split. Left: stacked bar chart with focal series highlighted. Right: hero stat + mix-shift callout + narrative + callout band.

families.description: What drove the change — contribution bars showing which categories added or subtracted from a total.

signals: prompt names a total that grew or shrank and lists what contributed
has 'contributed', 'drove growth', 'offset by', 'net change'
categories have positive and negative contributions that sum to a net delta

emphasis_question.prompt: What should land first — the drivers or the headline number?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If biggest contributor → driver-hero. If total change → headline-hero. If full decomposition → balanced.

options.label: Full decomposition
options.description: Bridge endpoints + contribution bars + narrative — reader traces the whole walk

options.label: Lead driver
options.description: Biggest contributor is the hero stat — chart and narrative support it

options.label: Headline number
options.description: Net change is the hero — contribution bars are supporting context

variants.name: Bridge endpoints + contribution bars + narrative
variants.layout: 58/42 split. Left: bridge panel (start → end with delta) + diverging contribution bars with net total. Right: hero stat + mix-shift + narrative + callout band.

variants.name: Lead driver callout with compact decomposition
variants.layout: Left 40%: hero stat (lead driver) + mix-shift badge + narrative. Right 60%: compact bridge + contribution bars. Summary band at bottom.

families.description: Two parallel workstreams tracked side by side — internal readiness vs client adoption, build vs rollout.

signals: prompt tracks two distinct but related workstreams in parallel
has 'track 1 / track 2', 'internal + external', 'build + adopt'
each track has its own completion metric or milestone status

emphasis_question.prompt: Are the two tracks equally important, or is one the bottleneck?
emphasis_question.detect_from: If one track done and other is focus → handoff. If both equal → parallel. If showing overall program → program.

options.label: Two equal tracks
options.description: Both tracks shown side by side with matching visual weight

options.label: Handoff moment
options.description: Track A is done — the slide is about transitioning focus to Track B

options.label: Program overview
options.description: Both tracks feed a shared objective — the goal card is the hero

variants.name: Side-by-side track panels with KPI chips
variants.layout: Full-width. Two side-by-side section panels. Left: journey timeline + detail grid + next-phase cards. Right: item list + objective card. Summary bar at bottom.

variants.name: Completed track compact + active track hero
variants.layout: Left 35%: compact completed-track summary. Right 65%: active track as hero — timeline, current items, next actions. Goal card at bottom.

variants.name: Shared goal hero with compact track strips
variants.layout: Hero goal card at top. Below: two compact track strips showing milestone status + KPI. Summary bar at bottom.
